$comment: Gemfall beat 7, the Collection's chapter 7 (docs/campaigns/gemfall.md, 7H). Defines facet_caravan, which 07r and 07l also grant. Summit: scene_tree_line's two choices set climbed_the_mountain or walked_away; the lost-fight setback sets climbed_the_mountain. Cult and clock are both decided once, at scene_tamsins_offer: sell (funded_the_break + clock_late), refuse (refused_the_cult), or hand the stones back (refused_the_cult + clock_steady). The setback path never reaches that scene and sets clock_late itself. The Walk is the Collection's own exit from the campaign, and it lives here: after the tree line a walking party plays the epilogue in this chapter (the walk_ scenes) and its endings carry endsCampaign, so the campaign completes without a chapter 8. A walking party never enters the mountain.
title: The Collection

objectives.label: Won the Caravan Stone at the worst bend
Gave a stone back, even though nobody made you
Saw that the gem deposit was really a crab

facet_caravan.name: The Caravan Stone
facet_caravan.text: The masterpiece stone of the fattest caravan. It hums so loud the mules wear earmuffs.

scene_like_weather.narration: The realm reads you now. Hedges grow slower as you pass. A mosshorn on the ridge sniffs your packs and quietly leaves. The warrens go silent for a mile around you, and the silence follows you like a dog that nobody is feeding. Up ahead, every road funnels into the Pinch, one gap between two red hills, and somewhere in it is the next stone on your list.

choices.label: Listen to what the silence is saying

scene_like_weather_listen_silence.narration: Your bigfoot stops and listens to the silence the way other people listen to a song. It has a shape. It is a circle, a mile wide, and you are standing in the exact middle of it. "They're not frightened of us," your bigfoot says. "They're frightened of what we've got." The silence agrees.

choice_the_race.narration: Three other crowds want the same stones you do: wardens with numbered boxes, grandmothers with knitting, and people in bark masks with sacks. You need to get ahead of all of them. How?

choices.label: Show the wardens your citadel pass
Nobody knows what you are for. Use that.
Push into the camps and start trading

choice_the_race_camps.narration: You push straight into the camps and start trading. Your first deal is a stone for a honeycake, which should not have worked and did. Your second is a stone for a story about the first one. By the third deal, people are coming to find you.

choice_the_race_nobody_knows.narration: Nobody knows what you are for, so nobody stops you. A warden with a numbered box walks straight past. A grandmother nods to you as if you were one of hers. A mask offers you soup. You take the soup. Everybody at the Pinch thinks you are somebody else's problem, which is exactly where you want to be.

scene_warden_pass.narration: You told the wardens the truth at the citadel, and they still trust you. A clerk stamps your pass and waves you through without looking in your bags. The stamp feels heavy on your hand all afternoon.

scene_grandmother_look.narration: A grandmother looks at your bulging packs over her knitting for a long, long time. She does not say "No, dear." She does not say anything at all. Then she hands you a warm bead, because it is cold up there.

choices.label: Put one stone in her knitting basket

scene_grandmother_look_give_one.narration: You put one stone in her knitting basket. The needles stop. "Thank you, dear," she says, and for a moment her voice is not the knitting voice at all. She digs out a second warm bead and presses it into your palm. "One for the one you gave," she says. Then the needles start again.

scene_grandmother_look_thank.narration: You thank her and walk on. She says nothing. Her needles click a little faster. Twenty paces on, you realise she has not stopped looking at your packs, and that she has not blinked.

scene_road_gifts.narration: The trading is fast and loud and everybody is shouting prices. And in the middle of it, the road starts bringing things back to you: things you did on the way here, walking up the hill on their own legs, as if the whole realm had been keeping your receipts.

choices.label: A flat boat is coming up the dry creek
A MossHome runner is waving a knotted cord
A boggart is sidling up with a satchel
A boggart is sidling up with a satchel
Someone in a pointed hat is pushing to the front

scene_ossley.narration: A frog in a very old hat is poling a flat boat up a creek with no water in it: Old Ossley, the ferryman from Stone Crossing, with a boat piled with every stone the river took off somebody this season. "Stones want to go home," he says. "We only kept them until someone was going that way." He looks at your packs for a long time. "Which way are you going?"

choices.label: Ask what you still owe him from the river
Let him pole on up the mountain

scene_ossley_debt.narration: Ossley takes a long time to answer, which is how Ossley answers. His price is not coin. It never was. "One stone you didn't find," he says. "Give it to the boat. That's all."

choices.label: Choose a stone and put it in his boat

scene_mosshome_runner.narration: A MossHome runner jogs up with a string of grumbling mules, loaded with everything the Woods confiscated from careless hunters. She counts the knots on your cord. Then she looks at your packs, and counts them again, slower.

choices.label: Claim everything the cord is owed
Tell her to take the stones back to the Woods

scene_mosshome_runner_send_home.narration: "Take the stones back to the Woods," you say. The runner stares. Then she grins so wide the moss in her hair shifts, ties a new knot in your cord, and turns the mules round on the spot. "The record will like that," she calls over her shoulder, already jogging. "The record likes a surprise."

scene_mosshome_runner_claim.narration: You claim everything the cord is owed. The runner unloads it all, every shovel and hat and humming stone, and counts your packs again as she does it, slower each time. "The record will know who has these," she says, which is what she was told to say, and jogs off without looking back.

scene_boggart.narration: A boggart with a satchel full of scribbled paper sidles up, not looking at you, and says to nobody: "Catalogue. Who bought what in the marsh. Very useful, for a collector. Costs one really good sentence you overheard."

choices.label: Tell it what a warden said about acceptable losses
Tell it what Grandmother Tull said about the unused bell

scene_boggart_grandma_said.narration: You tell it what Grandmother Tull said about the bell nobody rings, word for word, including the second time she said it. The boggart closes its eyes to listen and keeps them closed for some time afterwards. "Lovely," it says to nobody. "Lovely." The catalogue is in your hands before you notice it has let go.

scene_boggart_wardens_said.narration: "Acceptable losses," you repeat, in the captain's exact voice. The boggart shivers all over with delight and writes it down twice, once forwards and once backwards. "Oh, that's a good one. That's a keeper." It hands over the catalogue without ever once looking at you.

scene_ford_witch.narration: It is Mother Thrum, the ford witch from the caravan queue, with her wool-wrapped stone still ringing under one arm. She looks at your packs, and then at you, and then at your packs again. "I am still asking," she says. "What do you actually want?"

scene_ford_witch_dont_know.narration: "I don't know any more," you say. Mother Thrum's face softens for the first time since the ford. She keeps the stone, and ties a songbird ribbon round your wrist instead. "That's the first true thing anyone's said to me on this hill," she says. "I'll ask again. I always do."

scene_ford_witch_all_of_them.narration: "All of them," you say. Mother Thrum does not sigh, which is worse than if she had. She unwraps the Ford Stone and puts it in your hands, still ringing. "Then here is one more," she says. "Mind it doesn't ring you to sleep." It does not stop ringing. Not for you.

scene_evening.narration: Evening. Campfires pop up all along the road, and the ground keeps shrugging, a little more often than this morning. Nobody pitches a tent within a stone's throw of yours.

choices.label: A centaur relay is cantering past your camp
Listen to the singers at the campfires
An Exchange caravan rolls in, and someone is waving

scene_centaur_relay.narration: The centaur relay canters past your fire and does not stop. They have heard what you are for now. "Fat caravan tomorrow," one calls over her shoulder. "We're sending it the long way. Round you."

choices.label: Call after her, the old road-people way

scene_centaur_relay_fair.narration: "Fair enough," you say. She looks surprised that you did not argue, and slows to a trot for a few paces as if she might say something else. Then she does not, and the relay canters on into the dark, and the dust settles on your humming packs.

scene_centaur_relay_old_way.narration: You call after her the old road-people way, palm up, from far off, the way your family has done for longer than roads. She pulls up so hard she skids. For a long moment she looks at you, a manticore keeping the old courtesy while carrying what you carry. "Fine," she says at last. "Past you. Once. Don't make me sorry."

scene_relay_sing.narration: The relay singers have new verses about wagons that have not arrived yet, so you can hear tomorrow's traffic tonight. Then a grandmother's runner hands you a list of caves nobody may ever dig. For a collector, it looks a lot like a treasure map.

scene_ember.narration: "Darlings! From the docks!" Madame Coralie Fenn is lashed to the top of the caravan in her barrel on wheels, waving with both arms. She remembers you fondly. She also remembers the Ember Facet you sold her, which is right here in a velvet box, and its price has gone up a very great deal since then.

choices.label: Buy it back. It belongs in the collection.

scene_ember_too_much.narration: You wave. Madame Fenn waves back with both arms and the barrel wobbles alarmingly on its lashings. "Next time, darlings!" she calls, and the caravan rolls on toward the camps with your very first stone humming in a velvet box on top of it. You watch until the lanterns turn the corner.

scene_ember_buy_back.narration: You pay what Madame Fenn asks, which is a great deal, and she counts it twice and hugs the velvet box before she hands it over. "I always hoped it would be you, darlings," she says, and seems to mean it. The Ember Facet is warm as toast, exactly as you remember, and it hums as if it remembers you too.

rest_lonely_camp.narration: Your camp is very quiet. Nobody else's is. The stones in your packs hum all together, low and sleepy, like a cat that is far too big. Patch each other up. Tomorrow is the worst bend in the north road.

scene_roadside_glitter.narration: Just before the bend, two big glittering lumps sit on a warm patch of road. Prospectors keep trying to pick them up, and keep coming back very quickly without them. The lumps look exactly like gem deposits. They also have legs, if you look.

choices.label: Watch them carefully before doing anything
That is a gem deposit. Grab it!
Follow the trail of tiny tied grass knots around them

check_crabs.prompt: Read what the glittering lumps are trying to tell you

onSuccess.narration: They are glassback crabs, and they are waving their claws in the most polite warning in the realm: this is our warm spot. You walk the long way round, and they wave you off like aunties.

onFailure.narration: You step a little closer to get a better look, which turns out to be exactly the wrong thing to do.

encounter_crabs.narration: The gem deposits stand up. They are glassback crabs, and this is their warm spot, and they would like you off it.

onVictory.narration: The crabs decide the warm spot was overrated anyway, and clatter off sideways into the rocks, grumbling.

onDefeat.narration: The crabs shove you clean off the road and into a ditch. By the time you climb out, half your packs have burst open, and the masks are already scooping up what rolled out.

choice_the_bend.narration: The worst bend in the north road: a hairpin over a long drop. Here comes the fattest caravan in the funnel. Wardens are waiting with boxes, grandmothers with knitting, masks with sacks, and you. Four crowds, one wagon, and in the middle of it the Caravan Stone, humming.

choices.label: You heard this caravan in last night's song. Be there first.
The relay owes you one. Ask them to bring it your way.
You know from the catalogue who bought it, and for how much
Get the other three crowds arguing with each other
Notice the middle wagon's wheel is about to come off
Flash your warden pass and walk right up to the wagon
Slip in while everyone else is shouting
Make the caravan master an offer

choice_the_bend_axle.narration: Your bigfoot has been listening to the silence, and the silence has a wobble in it. The middle wagon's wheel is about to come off. You say so, loudly, just as it does, and while three crowds jump back from the lurching wagon, you are the one standing still enough to catch what rolls out.

choice_the_bend_crowd.narration: Your kitsune says one quiet thing to a warden about grandmothers, and one quiet thing to a grandmother about masks, and one quiet thing to a mask about wardens. Thirty seconds later all three crowds are shouting at each other across the road, and the middle wagon is standing quite alone, with you beside it.

choice_the_bend_buyers.narration: You know from the boggart's catalogue exactly who bought this stone and for how much, and you say both numbers out loud before the caravan master has finished climbing down. She goes pale. Then she laughs. "Well," she says. "No point haggling with somebody who's read my post."

choice_the_bend_relay_owes.narration: The relay owes you one, and the relay pays its debts. The fattest caravan in the funnel comes round the hairpin on the wrong side of the road, straight to where you are standing, and the centaur leading it does not look at you once. "Once," she says to the air, and is gone.

choice_the_bend_early.narration: You heard this caravan in last night's verse, and you are at the hairpin an hour before anyone, sitting on the rock the lead wagon has to stop at. When it stops, the caravan master looks at you, then at the wardens and grandmothers and masks still puffing up the road behind, and shrugs. "First come," she says.

check_bend.prompt: Outbid three other crowds for one humming wagon

onSuccess.narration: Your offer is so good, and so fast, that the caravan master shakes your hand before anybody else has finished shouting.

onFailure.narration: While you are still counting, a masked wagoneer quietly steers the middle wagon off up a side track. The Caravan Stone is gone, and the masks have it.

scene_caravan_won.narration: The Caravan Stone is the size of a loaf of bread and hums like a whole choir. You put it in the pack with the others, and every stone you own hums louder, all together, as if they recognise each other. The ground shakes, just once, in reply.

choices.label: Make camp below the tree line

scene_tamsins_offer.narration: That night a woman in a bark mask sits down at your fire and takes it off. It is Hessa, from the soup tent. "We'll buy the lot," she says sweetly. "Every stone. You'd be rich, and we'd break the seal properly, all at once, so it can be fixed properly." She sets out the money in little piles, and it is a lot of little piles.

scene_sold.narration: Hessa counts out every coin with great care, and thanks you, and means it. As she carries the stones away into the dark, the ground shakes once, hard, and does not stop for a long time. Down the hill, a bell rope creaks against its ribbon.

choices.label: Walk on to the tree line

scene_handed_back.narration: Hessa puts her mask back on and goes. In the morning you carry the stones to the grandmothers' cairn and set them down one by one, and a grandmother wraps each in wool. Strangely, your packs still feel heavy afterwards, as if the stones left their shape behind.

choices.label: Walk on to the tree line

choice_tree_line.narration: The tree line. Above it, the mountain, shaking in a slow, patient rhythm. Below it, the road south, and everybody else on it, running. There is not one embermoth left in the foothills. Up, or down?

rest_the_climb.narration: You walk up the mountain everyone else is running away from. Somewhere at the top is the eighth stone, the one that is not for sale. The ground shakes under every step, and your packs hum louder the higher you go, as if the stones know exactly where they are.

ending_robbed.narration: The masks are gone, and so is the fattest caravan, and so is half your collection. The ground is shaking in a slow, patient rhythm now. You gather what is left and climb, because the only stone left worth having is at the top, and you are a long way behind.

walk_scene_tree_line.narration: You turn south. Above you the mountain shakes in its slow, patient rhythm. Below you is the green, and everybody else running into it. Your packs are so full of humming stones that the three of you sound like a walking beehive, and a passing drover gives you a very wide berth.

choices.label: Let the Caravan Stone hum the loudest, all the way down

walk_scene_tree_line_caravan_hum.narration: You let the Caravan Stone hum the loudest, all the way down, as if it were leading. Behind you, once, the mountain answers it: a single long note you feel through your boots rather than hear. Then the stone hums on, and the mountain does not answer again.

walk_scene_realm_reads.narration: The realm reads you as you go. Jackalopes go silent a mile ahead of you. A pride of manticores walks a wide, polite circle around your camp. Even the moss leans away from the path. Everything that can hear the stones steps aside, like you are weather.

choices.label: Ask the trees, kindly, why they are leaning away
Hold up the Glade Stone and let the forest hear it

walk_scene_realm_reads_glade_hum.narration: You hold up the Glade Stone and let the forest hear it. Every leaf within a hundred paces goes still at once. Not a rustle. Not a bird. The forest has recognised the sound of its own bruise, and it holds its breath until you put the stone away.

walk_scene_realm_reads_ask_trees.narration: Your unicorn asks the trees, kindly, why they lean away. The answer comes slowly, in creaks. It is not you, they say. It is what you carry, and where it is going, which is away. The trees do not sound angry. They sound like somebody watching a cart go the wrong way and deciding not to shout.

walk_rest_switchback.narration: You camp on a switchback where the rocks are still warm from the day. Nobody says much. Share out the last of the snacks, patch each other up, and listen to the mountain grumbling behind you, far away and getting farther.

walk_scene_factions.narration: On the caravan road, a centaur relay runner called Brisk is coming up as you go down. She slows to a trot. "News," she says, "if you want it. Everybody up there is doing something." She looks at your packs. "Without you."

choices.label: Ask how the wardens are doing
Ask how the grandmothers are doing
Ask whether anybody knows what you know

walk_scene_factions_close.narration: "Does anybody up there know what we know?" Brisk looks at you very hard. "You knew," she says. "You knew and you came down." She does not say anything else. She does not have to.

walk_scene_wardens_hold.narration: "The wardens did what you told them," says Brisk. "Checkpoints on every road. Every stone confiscated and logged twice. It's working. It's ugly to watch. But they're holding." A warden wagon rolls past, uphill, full of stones going home.

walk_scene_gatherers_hold.narration: "The grandmothers turned gathering law inside out," says Brisk. "Every stone that came down is going back up, carried by dragonlings with bells on their tails. It's slow. It's holding." Somewhere above you, a very small bell jingles past.

walk_scene_news.narration: "Nobody knows much," says Brisk. "The wardens are guessing. The cult is singing. The dragon is being a dragon. Everybody's waiting for somebody to do something." She looks at your packs, then at you, and does not say anything else, which for a centaur is very loud.

walk_scene_boundary.narration: At the boundary stones, a dragonling grandmother sits on the oldest stone, knitting something long and red. She looks at your humming packs. "Take what the mountain drops," she says. "Never pry at what it holds." Then she holds out one hand, palm up, and waits.

choices.label: Put a stone in her hand
Tell her who you sold stones to
Ask her why the bells keep ringing
Ask her why her knitting needles are shaking

walk_scene_boundary_thank.narration: You thank her, and keep walking. Her hand stays out, palm up, for a long time after you have passed. You know this because you look back, and you wish you had not.

walk_scene_boundary_give.narration: You put a stone in her hand. She closes her fingers round it and holds it against the long red knitting as if warming it. "Take what the mountain drops," she says, more softly this time. "Thank you, dear." Behind you, a small bell rings a ring you have not heard before, and it is a happy one.

walk_scene_the_fuse.narration: The grandmother puts her knitting down. Up on the mountain the bells are counting, every town at once. "Everybody knows what the last ring means," she says. "Nobody says it." She does not say it either. She just looks at you for a long time, and then knits faster.

choices.label: Put a stone in her hand after all

walk_scene_the_fuse_give.narration: You put a stone in her hand after all. She looks at it, and at you, and the needles stop shaking for exactly as long as it takes her to tuck it into her apron. "Well," she says. "That's one." Then she picks up the knitting again, and the bells go on counting.

walk_scene_look_back.narration: At the bottom of the foothills you turn round, one last time. Mount Red Sky glows against the evening sky. Somebody up there is doing the thing you decided not to do.

choices.label: Send word back up the mountain, everything you know
Watch the embermoths settle back on the warm rocks
Listen: the grandmother's bell, ringing the happy ring

walk_check_send_word.prompt: Get a message about the seal back up the mountain in time

onSuccess.narration: A griffin courier takes your letter straight up into the smoke. By morning, the warden checkpoints are reading it aloud.

onFailure.narration: Your letter goes up with a caravan that turns round halfway, because caravans do that now.

walk_check_last_chance.prompt: Give your best stone to a dragonling runner heading uphill, and ask them to hurry

onSuccess.narration: The runner takes your stone and your message, and runs. You never learn their name. They get there.

onFailure.narration: The runner is kind, and quick, and just too late.

walk_ending_collectors.narration: You walk out of the foothills rich, and the realm holds. Not because of you, but it holds. The last bell never rings. Back home, people ask where you got all those stones, and some of them ask the troll's old question: and where is it going? You are still thinking about the answer. History files you as The Collectors, and leaves the page after it blank, in case.

walk_ending_not_there.narration: Behind you, the last bell rings. You are a long way down the road when the mountain shrugs, and you watch the red sky grow redder from somewhere safe. The realm goes on, rearranged, and history files you as The Ones Who Weren't There. But in your pack, one stone has stopped humming. It is pointing north, like a compass, as if it is asking whether you would like to try again.

llmHints.tone: warm, glittering, a little lonely; the land treating the party like weather, never scolding; after the Walk: quiet, bittersweet, honest; the realm is never cruel to the walkers, it just tells the truth; always a spark at the end
forbidden: calling the party greedy or bad

npcVoices.hessa: Deep Hollow cell member who ran the soup tent; sweet, sincere, makes the arithmetic sound kind; says 'properly' a lot
npcVoices.old_ossley: very few words, long pauses that are not hesitation, answers the question you meant
npcVoices.grandmother: a dragonling grandmother at the boundary stones; knits, quotes the one rule, never says the thing everyone knows
npcVoices.mosshome_runner: breathless, cheerful, counts knots out loud, then counts packs
npcVoices.boggart: talks sidelong to nobody, never meets your eye, treasures overheard sentences
npcVoices.ford_witch: Mother Thrum, the ford witch; pointed hat, dry, kind underneath; only asks one question and means it
npcVoices.centaur_relay: brisk, proud of the roads, speaks over her shoulder at a canter
npcVoices.exchange_merchant: Madame Coralie Fenn, the Exchange gem-buyer in a barrel on wheels; delighted to see you, genuinely fond, calls everyone darlings, and still a merchant
npcVoices.caravan_master: exhausted, practical, will sell to whoever stops shouting first
npcVoices.brisk: Brisk, a centaur relay runner; fast-talking, fair, says a lot by saying nothing
